draft.title: Proposed Evaluation Framework for Corey Wilks, Psy.D. Public Site Capture
draft.question: What observable behaviors, decisions, and judgments can be evaluated from the public website capture to assess the creator's communication, positioning, and service clarity?

dimensions.name: Positioning clarity
dimensions.note: How clearly the site communicates the target audience, problem addressed, and unique approach.
observable_manifestations: Explicitly names target audience (founders, leaders, creators)
States the core problem (psychological bottlenecks)
Describes the approach (inner game, psychological, existential, identity-level)
Uses consistent terminology across headings and excerpts
evidence: I work with founders, leaders, and creators who are already getting results but know they’re capable of more.
My job is the inner game—the deeply psychological, existential, and identity-level aspects still capping your potential.
Remove the Psychological Bottlenecks Costing You Business Growth.

dimensions.name: Offer differentiation
dimensions.note: How the site distinguishes the creator's services from generic coaching or productivity advice.
observable_manifestations: Emphasizes depth beyond surface-level tips
References specific frameworks (e.g., Four Horsemen of Fear)
Highlights psychological expertise (Psy.D., psychologist turned coach)
Positions services as addressing underlying patterns
evidence: He doesn't just address surface-level productivity tips; he goes deeper into understanding the fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating.
Corey has the skill to consistently get underneath the surface problem to the real one.
The Four Horsemen of Fear framework completely transformed the way I operate in my life and business.

dimensions.name: Evidence use
dimensions.note: How the site uses testimonials, credentials, and media mentions to support claims.
observable_manifestations: Includes testimonials from named individuals with roles
Lists media appearances (podcasts, publications)
Mentions credentials (Psy.D., psychologist)
Uses phrases like 'As Seen In' and 'Trusted By'

The Modern Wisdom Podcast with Chris Williamson
As Seen In: Trusted By:

dimensions.name: Content depth and topical range
dimensions.note: The breadth and depth of topics covered in articles and podcasts, as indicated by titles and descriptions.
observable_manifestations: Article titles address psychological concepts (e.g., Imposter Syndrome, fear, self-sabotage)
Podcast episodes feature notable guests
Topics go beyond productivity to identity and existential themes
Offers free masterclass and newsletter

dimensions.name: Call-to-action clarity
dimensions.note: How clearly the site directs visitors to take specific actions (subscribe, enroll, book).
observable_manifestations: Clear CTAs like 'Subscribe now', 'Work with me', 'Click here to learn more'
Multiple entry points for engagement (newsletter, masterclass, program enrollment)
Service offerings are listed with descriptions

Work with me ↗

dimensions.name: Tone and language consistency
dimensions.note: Consistency in tone (professional, psychological, non-hyperbolic) across the site copy.
observable_manifestations: Uses psychological terminology consistently
Avoids hyperbolic claims in article titles
Maintains a professional yet accessible tone
Repeated phrases like 'inner game' and 'psychological bottlenecks'
evidence: A non-hyperbolic, psychology-based understanding of what holds us back from self-actualization
The deeply psychological, existential, and identity-level aspects
Navigating the inner game of entrepreneurship.

dimensions.name: Social proof specificity
dimensions.note: The specificity and credibility of testimonials and media mentions.
observable_manifestations: Testimonials include full names and roles
Media mentions include specific podcast names
Testimonials describe concrete outcomes or insights
Some testimonials are vague (e.g., 'life-changing')

Jay Yang Entrepreneur, Author
The Modern Wisdom Podcast with Chris Williamson

dimensions.name: Transparency and compliance
dimensions.note: Presence of disclaimers, privacy policy, and affiliate disclosures.
observable_manifestations: Affiliate disclosure present
Terms of Service and Privacy Policy linked
Cookie consent notice present
Disclaimers policy mentioned

questions.text: Describe a recent situation where you had to explain your coaching approach to a potential client. What did you emphasize, and how did you differentiate yourself from other coaches?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the creator can articulate their unique value proposition in practice, not just on the website.

questions.text: Can you give an example of a time you used a specific psychological framework (like the Four Horsemen of Fear) with a client? What observable change did you notice?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the creator can translate their marketed frameworks into concrete client work.

questions.text: Tell me about a podcast or article you published that received strong feedback. What did you do to ensure the content was both psychologically accurate and accessible?
questions.what_it_tests: How the creator balances depth and accessibility in their content.

questions.text: Walk me through how you decide which services to offer (e.g., 1:1 coaching, workshops, intensive). What signals from your audience influence those decisions?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether service offerings are based on observed audience needs or assumptions.

questions.text: Describe a time a client's testimonial or feedback surprised you. How did you incorporate that feedback into your work?
questions.what_it_tests: How the creator uses social proof and feedback to improve their offerings.

questions.text: What steps do you take to ensure your marketing claims (e.g., 'life-changing') are not overpromising? Can you give a specific example?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the creator is aware of the gap between marketing language and actual outcomes.

questions.text: How do you handle situations where a client's issue falls outside your expertise? Can you describe a specific instance?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the creator maintains professional boundaries and refers out when needed.

questions.text: Can you share an example of how you measure the effectiveness of your coaching or programs beyond testimonials?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the creator has systematic ways to evaluate impact, not just anecdotal evidence.

recommended_interventions: Clarify the specific outcomes clients can expect from each service, using observable metrics where possible.
Provide more detailed case studies or anonymized examples of client work to substantiate claims.
Add a section that explicitly addresses the creator's scope of practice and referral process.
Develop a system for collecting and reporting outcome data beyond testimonials.
Review marketing language to ensure it aligns with the non-hyperbolic tone used in article titles.
reporting.re_test: Re-test after 6 months by capturing the same URL and comparing changes in positioning, evidence, and service descriptions.

draft.claim_boundary: All dimensions are based solely on the public website capture. No claims are made about actual client outcomes, creator credentials beyond stated, or effectiveness of services. Testimonials are marketing language and not verified.
missing_evidence: No evidence of specific client outcomes or measurable results.
No evidence of the creator's actual credentials beyond the title 'Psy.D.' and 'psychologist turned coach'.
No evidence of the creator's decision-making process or internal judgments.
No evidence of how the creator handles ethical dilemmas or referrals.
No evidence of the creator's content creation process or audience research.

draft.title: Draft Evaluation Framework for Psychology-Informed Entrepreneurship Coaching
draft.question: How clearly and credibly does the public-site capture communicate an observable coaching approach for helping founders, leaders, and creators identify and act on psychological or decision-related barriers to business growth?

dimensions.name: Target-user and problem clarity
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether the site identifies who the work is for and describes a recognizable problem or decision context. This is a communication hypothesis, not evidence that the stated problem exists or is widespread.
observable_manifestations: Names the intended users or roles.
Describes specific situations such as procrastination, overthinking, self-doubt, or difficulty making decisions.
Connects the stated problem to business, leadership, publishing, or growth activity.
Avoids relying only on broad claims such as reaching one's potential.
evidence: "founders, leaders, and creators"
"psychological bottlenecks costing you business growth"
"procrastination, Imposter Syndrome, perfectionism, overthinking, constant self-doubt"

dimensions.name: Observable coaching process
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether the site makes the proposed work inspectable as a sequence of actions, conversations, or decisions rather than only as an outcome claim.
observable_manifestations: Explains what happens during coaching, workshops, or strategy sessions.
Identifies how a client moves from a stated business question to a next decision or action.
Distinguishes ongoing coaching from focused sessions and educational content.
States what evidence or client behavior would indicate progress.
evidence: "Ongoing coaching to dive deep into what's holding you back, what you actually want, and how to achieve it."
"A focused 3-hour session for founders and leaders ready to work through what's costing them growth."
"leave understanding the pattern in me that created it"

dimensions.name: Depth of inquiry and reframing
dimensions.note: Evaluates the stated emphasis on examining underlying patterns, fears, or assumptions. The interpretation that this produces better decisions remains a hypothesis for creator review.
observable_manifestations: Invites examination of the pattern behind a business question.
Reframes fear or uncertainty as information to examine rather than an automatic stop signal.
Connects inner reflection to a concrete leadership, publishing, or operating decision.
Separates a proposed framework from proof of its effectiveness.
evidence: "get underneath the surface problem to the real one"
"the pattern in me that created it"
"transform your relationship with fear"
"Imposter Syndrome wasn't a sign to back off"

dimensions.name: Action orientation
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether the framework translates psychological or existential reflection into observable behavior, iteration, or follow-through.
observable_manifestations: Defines a specific action following reflection or coaching.
Addresses publishing, iterating, choosing, or making a decision.
Treats progress as observable behavior rather than an internal identity claim.
Includes a way to review whether the action was attempted and what was learned.
evidence: "fears that prevent us from publishing and iterating"
"how I lead, how I make decisions"
"how to achieve it"
"The Action Gap"

dimensions.name: Offer and pathway clarity
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether a prospective user can distinguish the available formats and select an appropriate entry point.
observable_manifestations: Clearly differentiates 1:1 coaching, workshops or keynotes, focused sessions, and educational programs.
States the intended use case for each offer.
Provides a coherent path from free material to a paid or direct service without implying that enrollment proves effectiveness.
Makes scope, duration, and expected participant activity explicit.
evidence: "1:1 Coaching"
"Workshops & Keynotes"
"Audit + Strategy Session"
"Get the Psychology of Success Masterclass for free"

dimensions.name: Evidence and claim calibration
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether testimonials and promotional statements are presented as bounded reports rather than general proof of outcomes.
observable_manifestations: Labels testimonials as individual accounts.
Separates reported experience from independently verified outcome evidence.
Avoids treating terms such as life-changing or transformational as measurable findings.
States what the site does and does not establish about effectiveness.
evidence: "What People Say About Me and My Work"
"life-changing"
"transformational"
"I've been in and around the coaching world for 20 years"

dimensions.name: Scope and boundary communication
dimensions.note: Evaluates whether the site clarifies the practical boundaries of psychology-informed coaching, including what the service is designed to address and what remains unspecified.
observable_manifestations: Describes the service as coaching rather than presenting coaching language alone as clinical care.
Clarifies the limits of the work when discussing fear, self-doubt, or Imposter Syndrome.
Identifies when a client should use a different type of support, if applicable.
Avoids implying that a framework can resolve every personal or business difficulty.
evidence: "PSYCHOLOGIST TURNED COACH"
"My job is the inner game"
"deeply psychological, existential, and identity-level aspects"
"life and business"

questions.text: When a prospective client arrives with a business problem such as delayed publishing or an unresolved decision, what observable steps does the coaching process use to identify the relevant pattern and choose a next action?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the stated depth of inquiry can be translated into a reviewable sequence of actions.

questions.text: What would a client do differently, in a specific work situation, after examining fear, perfectionism, overthinking, or self-doubt?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether claimed inner-game work has a defined behavioral manifestation.

questions.text: How are 1:1 coaching, the Audit + Strategy Session, workshops or keynotes, and the Inner Game Intensive distinguished by purpose, duration, and participant activity?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether users can select an offer based on observable needs and format.

questions.text: What evidence would you review to determine whether a client made progress beyond reporting that the work felt insightful or transformational?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether progress is assessed using observable decisions, actions, or outcomes rather than promotional language.

questions.text: Can you provide an example of a client-facing exercise or conversation that moves from a stated business question to a concrete decision?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the proposed method is sufficiently specific for creator calibration.

questions.text: What boundaries should a prospective client understand when the site discusses fear, Imposter Syndrome, self-doubt, or other psychological language?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the public communication distinguishes coaching scope from unsupported clinical or universal claims.

questions.text: Which statements on the site are intended as hypotheses, personal frameworks, or client reports rather than independently verified evidence?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether observed language is separated from evidentiary status.

questions.text: After a coaching conversation, how are an agreed action, review point, and learning from the result recorded or revisited?
questions.what_it_tests: Whether the service includes an observable feedback loop.

fields: Dimension rating: supported, partly supported, unsupported, or MISSING
Short site excerpt supporting the rating
Observed behavior, decision, or judgment being evaluated
Interpretation stated explicitly as a hypothesis
Reviewer notes on whether the public claim is appropriately calibrated
recommended_interventions: Add a concise example showing how a coaching conversation proceeds from a business question to a concrete action.
Differentiate each offer by purpose, format, duration, and expected participant activity.
Define how progress is observed or reviewed after coaching.
Label testimonials and transformational language as reported experiences rather than general proof.
Add clear scope language for psychology-related terms and clarify what the service does not claim to provide.
reporting.re_test: Re-review a revised public page using the same dimensions. Mark a dimension as supported only when the page provides a concrete process, behavior, decision, boundary, or evidence statement; otherwise retain partly supported, unsupported, or MISSING.

draft.claim_boundary: This framework is based only on the supplied single-page capture. It evaluates the clarity and reviewability of public claims, not the creator's competence, the quality or safety of services, client outcomes, causal effectiveness, audience characteristics, or clinical status. Testimonials are treated as reported statements, and promotional terms such as "life-changing" and "transformational" are not treated as proof. Interpretations about depth, action orientation, and scope are hypotheses for creator calibration.
missing_evidence: No detailed description of a coaching session, exercise, curriculum, or decision-making protocol.
No independently verified outcome data, comparison information, or defined success measures.
No information establishing how testimonials were collected, selected, or corroborated.
No stated boundaries describing when coaching is insufficient or when another form of support is appropriate.
No pricing, duration, eligibility, or participation requirements for the listed offers beyond the limited duration reference for the focused session.
No evidence in the capture showing how clients' actions or progress are tracked after coaching.
